## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Khettūpamapetavatthu* ("The Simile of a Field", Pv 1) is the opening story (*vatthu*) of the canonical *Petavatthu* [SuttaCentral; Norman 1983]. Unlike many stories in the collection that follow a conventional narrative dialogue between an observer and a suffering spirit (*peta*) recounting past misdeeds, the text appears to have been included simply because it incorporates the word *peta* [Norman 1983]. It conveys the teaching that arahants are like a fertile field wherein offerings can be planted, and that honouring arahants and *petas* is like planting seeds that will produce a corresponding karmic reward (*phala*) in due course [SuttaCentral; Norman 1983].
Translations of the text are cataloged in five languages on SuttaCentral, including an English version by Kovilo Bhikkhu [SuttaCentral].
Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus records any cross-language parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. In terms of internal Pali reuse, machine alignment via DharmaNexus records six matching passages with the commentary, the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (longest match spanning §1.1–4.4 of this text and §38_7–47 of the commentary) [DharmaNexus].
